convoLines.text: I'm not proud. I'm alive. Those two things stopped overlapping a while ago.
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Thao. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want to hear it? I dug it up. I was starving and your hole was right there. Happy now?"
"I'm not proud of how I survive. I'm just committed to it."
"I count what we have every morning. Numbers don't lie to you the way hope does."
"Still on wanting to survive, whatever it takes."
They glance away, then back. Different subject, same worry:
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"Jalen always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I can't reach this properly. Could you take a look?"
"It keeps getting worse. I can't haul or hunt with it like this — and if it festers, I'm done for. Please, clean it out and bind it tight."
You spend time tending them. This was care, not a promise of a cure.
"Still on that wound care."
"What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Jalen is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sleep's gone strange. I do push-ups at dawn at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Quinn grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"That again?" Pavel sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
The air goes tight. Their eyes narrow, just slightly.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
"Still on that wound care."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"I… What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
"A full night's sleep. Not safety, not answers — just eight hours where nothing needs me. That's my whole theology now. Forget it."
"Still on what you're hoping for. It'll pass."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I dreamed Jalen was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I said something cruel. I think about it every day."
"Thank you for hearing it. I needed someone to know — and I needed it to stop with you."
"You came through on this wound. I won't forget it."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Good. Then we're square." They look lighter for it.
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Jalen owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Quinn is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them American Persimmon — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About this wound — still need hands. Are you in?"
"I still need help with this wound."
You need to be right next to them, same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Since Jalen died... I keep expecting to see Jalen at the fire. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. Thao doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"The fire feels smaller without Jalen. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Quinn nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I check everyone's shoes for wear for Jalen, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Jalen Conti is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Jalen Conti is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Jalen kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Jalen's gone." Thao looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Jalen." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Riana blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Patient Aim (Level 1). One shot. You don't take the shot unless it's the shot.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Debris Shelter (Level 1). A lean-to of branches and leaves beats nothing. Dead air is insulation.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Cordage (Level 1). Twist plant fibers into string. Dogbane, nettle, yucca — strong fibers are everywhere.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Jalen Conti, 41 days. The mantle passes to Riana Shange.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Riana Shange, 53 — a trail crew lead. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Lucky Rock.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Jalen — and Jalen is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Thao, Quinn, Victor and 1 more speak for Riana — "Jalen trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Riana before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d52: Haven couldn't hold. On the fifth hungry day, people started walking — in different directions. The scattering, again.
d52: Borys spent the afternoon at the workbench, and the Crossbow bolt came apart in their hands. The materials are wasted.
d52: 📓 Codex: Quinn taught Thao Mediation.
d52: 🤒 Quinn is feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Rest and clean water — or it gets worse.

d52: 🌙 Raid — Thornfield came in the night from the southeast. They trampled 2 garden plots into mud. Nobody's dead, but the message is clear: the ground is theirs too, and they're done asking. (Trust -10
